title: Singleton augmentation under explicit subset insertion
statement: For every A,r,f,J as in [def-sc-principal-open-cech-subset-insertion], give the singleton inclusion D_S≤V and equality n=n+1-|S| for |S|=1. For s∈Γ(V,J^n), form the raw coordinate function which restricts s to singleton D_S, with the given degree transport, and is zero on every other subset. Its explicit insertion equals the tuple augmentation of the canonical restriction-section transport of s from [lem-sc-principal-open-cech-section-transport]. No coordinate comparison complex, differential hypothesis or choice of an abstract isomorphism is involved.

source.place: Tag 08C1, equation (20.40.0.1), and Tag 01FM (increasing tuples). Explicit coordinate verification written by V3, following the parent node steps 1 and 2; source read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08C1 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01FM.

proof.text: Evaluate the finite sum of additive insertion morphisms on the singleton-supported coordinate function, using homAddEquiv and finsetSum_apply. For |S|≠1 its insertion is zero by additivity. For |S|=1 apply the singleton component comparison, identifying this term with the common degree-zero extension inverse and total inclusion b applied to Pi.single t_S (z(t_S)).

Prove directly, coordinate by coordinate, that the sum over nonempty subsets of singleton-supported Pi.single terms equals z. At a tuple t the unique contributing subset is {t(0)}; card-one enumeration equals t. All other terms vanish. This also covers r=0 since there are no tuples. Commute b through the finite sum using map_sum. Cancel e.hom against e.inv using functoriality and Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc. The resulting degree-zero restriction followed by the (0,n) total inclusion is definitionally the alternating augmentation.

proof_origin.place: U3 Lean proof: direct singleton-summation argument and extension cancellation, with singleton transport isolated as lem-sc-principal-open-cech-singleton-augmentation-component. Keeps the original augmentation route.
